scenarios.stimulus: After a normal reset (i_a_valid=0 during reset and for the first cycle after release, i_a_intg_flip=0 and i_a_instr=0 throughout), do full-word writes with the PutPartialData opcode (a_opcode=1) instead of PutFullData. Each write uses a_size=2, a_mask=1111, a word-aligned register offset as the address, i_a_param=0 and its own a_source. In order: (1) PutPartialData to DIRECT_OUT with 32'hA5C3_0F96, then a full-word Get of DIRECT_OUT, MASKED_OUT_LOWER and MASKED_OUT_UPPER. (2) PutPartialData to DIRECT_OE with 32'h3C3C_C3C3, then a Get of DIRECT_OE. (3) PutPartialData to MASKED_OUT_UPPER with 32'hFFFF_1234 (mask field all ones), then a Get of DIRECT_OUT. (4) PutPartialData to PER_PIN_IO_0 with 32'h0000_0000 and to PER_PIN_OE_31 with 32'h0000_0000, then Gets of DIRECT_OUT and DIRECT_OE. (5) PutPartialData to INTR_ENABLE with 32'h0000_0000, then a Get of INTR_ENABLE. Keep i_d_ready=1 and i_gpio constant, and leave at least 4 idle cycles after each write response before the next write, so that o_gpio and o_gpio_en can be sampled. Expected values come from the contract: every write is a full-word write with mask 1111 and so succeeds (d_error=0), its response is AccessAck with d_size=2 and d_source echoed, readbacks equal the written values under the normal DIRECT/MASKED/PER_PIN semantics, o_gpio and o_gpio_en follow the DATA_OUT and DATA_OE model from 2 cycles after each response, and o_alert never pulses.

After reset, with i_a_intg_flip=0, i_a_instr=0, i_a_param=0, i_d_ready=1 and i_gpio constant, first write DIRECT_OUT=32'h0000_0000 with a normal full-word PutFullData (a_size=2, mask 1111). Then send these requests one by one, each with its own a_source, and read DIRECT_OUT with a normal full-word Get after each one. (a) Mask 1111 with size 0, marking inactive lanes as active: a Get with a_size=0 at address 0x14, and a PutPartialData with a_size=0 at address 0x14 and data 32'hFFFF_FFFF. Repeat both at 0x20 (DIRECT_OE, preloaded to 0). (b) Size 2 with a partial mask: Gets with a_size=2 at the word-aligned address 0x14 and masks 0011, 1100, 0001 and 1000. (c) Size-2 writes with a partial mask whose outcome does not depend on how the device treats them: first write DIRECT_OUT=32'h5A5A_5A5A with a normal full-word write. Then send PutFullData (a_size=2) and PutPartialData (a_size=2) to 0x14 with masks 0011 and 1100, all with data 32'h5A5A_5A5A, the value already stored. Expected values come from the contract. For (a), every request gets d_error=1, DIRECT_OUT and DIRECT_OE keep their values, and o_gpio and o_gpio_en do not change. For (b) and (c), check only that each request gets exactly one response with d_source and d_size echoed and d_opcode matching the request (AccessAckData for Get, AccessAck for Put). d_error and the data of these responses are not checked. DIRECT_OUT must read 32'h5A5A_5A5A after (c). Throughout: no o_alert pulse and o_d_intg_err=0.

unreachable.reason: The device accepts only one request at a time: it holds o_a_ready low from the moment it accepts a request until that request's response has been taken. So there can never be two accepted requests waiting for an answer, and never two A handshakes in consecutive cycles. The only edges where the host could repeat a handshake are the cycles straight after an acceptance, and a_ready is 0 then. The rules allow this. D-014 (GP-10-26) only says the host must not assume o_a_ready=1, and no rule makes the device take more than one request at a time. The host rules (GP-4.1-04, CHK-011 a) say a request must be held while a_ready is 0, so the test bench cannot force a second acceptance. Evidence: the existing outstanding/back-pressure test (CHK-038) and the random regression already queue hundreds of requests and drive them back to back with no gap. They do this with and without D-channel back-pressure, in both GpioAsyncOn settings. Neither point was hit.
